name: Memantine
route_note: Oral tablets, oral solution or once-daily extended-release capsules.
originator: Eli Lilly (synthesis); developed for dementia by Merz Pharma

discovery.note: First synthesised at Lilly in the 1960s; Merz later developed it for neurological use, and its NMDA antagonism was characterised in 1989.

tagline: NMDA receptor blocker for moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's disease
summary: Memantine is a low-affinity, uncompetitive NMDA glutamate receptor antagonist used for moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's disease. It is often combined with a cholinesterase inhibitor and offers modest symptomatic benefit.
mechanism: Memantine blocks the open NMDA receptor channel at the magnesium site with fast on–off kinetics. This is thought to reduce tonic, pathological glutamate activation that may contribute to neuronal dysfunction while preserving the brief, high-concentration glutamate signals needed for normal learning.
Like the related adamantane amantadine, it has some dopaminergic and 5-HT3 activity, but its clinical effect is attributed to NMDA receptor modulation.
uses: Moderate-to-severe dementia of the Alzheimer's type

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Memantine is first synthesised at Eli Lilly.

history.title: German launch
history.detail: Merz markets memantine in Germany (Akatinol) for dementia and other neurological conditions.

history.title: European approval
history.detail: The EU authorises Ebixa (Lundbeck) and Axura (Merz) for moderately severe to severe Alzheimer's disease.

history.title: Extended release
history.detail: Once-daily Namenda XR is approved in the US.

history.title: Namzaric
history.detail: A memantine/donepezil fixed-dose capsule is approved in the US.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic memantine tablets launch in the US.

pk.excretion: renal, mostly unchanged; elimination slowed by alkaline urine

facts: Memantine and the antiviral amantadine are both aminoadamantanes; memantine carries two extra methyl groups.
